title: Environments (Development, Staging, Production) and startup flow
hook: The ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT variable tells your app whether to show detailed errors, enable Swagger, or run strict production logging. Startup is the sequence from process launch until Kestrel accepts the first request.

blocks.text: ASP.NET Core uses the IHostEnvironment (and IWebHostEnvironment) abstraction to expose the current environment name: Development, Staging, Production, or a custom value. This name selects which appsettings.{Environment}.json file merges into configuration and drives conditional behavior in Program.cs — like enabling Swagger only in Development. Startup flow is everything from Main/Program entry through builder.Build(), middleware registration, and app.Run() until the host reports ApplicationStarted.

entries.plainDefinition: Environment variable that sets IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName. Defaults to Production if unset.
Local dev: detailed errors, Swagger, relaxed HTTPS, verbose logging.
Live deployment: generic error responses, no Swagger UI, structured logging, strict security headers.
entries.example: Kubernetes sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production in the deployment manifest.

entries.plainDefinition: Events for ApplicationStarted, ApplicationStopping, and ApplicationStopped during startup and shutdown.
entries.example: Register callback to flush Redis pub/sub subscriptions on shutdown.

blocks.text: Shipping with Development environment in Docker exposes stack traces and Swagger to the internet — a common security finding. Staging should mirror Production configuration but point at test databases and Redis clusters. Understanding startup order helps debug slow cold starts behind an API gateway: service provider build, EF migrations, Redis connection warmup, and Kestrel bind each add latency before the readiness probe passes.

blocks.title: Default is Production
blocks.body: If ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT is unset, the host assumes Production. That is safer for accidental deploys but surprises developers who forget to set Development locally.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Process starts
items.body: dotnet MyApi.dll or container ENTRYPOINT launches the runtime.

items.title: CreateBuilder
items.body: Configuration sources chain: json files, env vars, secrets. Environment name is read.

items.title: Service registration
items.body: DI container graph built — DbContext, Redis, HTTP clients registered.

items.title: Build + pipeline
items.body: Middleware chain assembled; conditional branches run based on IsDevelopment().

items.title: Run
items.body: Kestrel binds, IHostedServices start, ApplicationStarted fires, readiness probe can pass.

diagram.title: Environment-driven startup branches
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  Start[Process launch] --> Env{ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT}
  Env -->|Development| DevCfg[appsettings.Development.json\nSwagger + detailed errors]
  Env -->|Staging| StgCfg[appsettings.Staging.json\ntest Redis + DB]
  Env -->|Production| ProdCfg[appsettings.Production.json\nstrict logging]
  DevCfg --> Build[builder.Build]
  StgCfg --> Build
  ProdCfg --> Build
  Build --> Run[app.Run Kestrel + workers]
  Run --> Ready[/health ready]

snippet.label: Environment-conditional middleware
snippet.explanation: IsDevelopment() gates developer-only features. Production uses exception handler middleware that does not leak internals to API clients.

snippet.label: Custom Staging environment in Docker Compose
snippet.code:
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  api:
    image: order-api:latest
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Staging
      ConnectionStrings__OrdersDb: "Host=postgres-staging;Database=orders"
      Redis__Connection: "redis-staging:6379"
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
snippet.explanation: Staging uses production-like settings but different connection strings. Health check gates dependent services and load balancer registration.

snippet.label: Startup timing and lifetime hooks
snippet.explanation: Log startup duration to catch slow Redis or EF initialization before readiness probes timeout in Kubernetes.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Leaving ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development in production Kubernetes manifests. Using Staging connection strings in Production because the wrong appsettings file shipped. Running EF Migrate() on every startup in Production without a migration strategy. Forgetting that IsProduction() is the negation of Development and Staging — use explicit checks for Staging-only behavior.

interviewTakeaways: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT selects config files and conditional middleware; default is Production when unset.
Development enables Swagger and detailed errors; Production uses exception handlers and HSTS — never ship Dev to public endpoints.
In production, log startup duration and wire IHostApplicationLifetime for graceful Redis and queue drain on SIGTERM.

60s: Env var sets Development, Staging, or Production. Merges appsettings.{Env}.json. IsDevelopment gates Swagger. Default Production. Startup is CreateBuilder, services, Build, pipeline, Run. ApplicationStarted when ready for probes.
Follow-up: how do you prevent Swagger from being exposed in a misconfigured Production deploy?
commonPitfalls: Deploying with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development — exposes stack traces and Swagger publicly.
Treating NODE_ENV and ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT as identical — .NET defaults to Production, Node often assumes development.
Strong answer: 'Env drives config merge and middleware branches. Staging mirrors prod infra with test data. Log startup time. ApplicationStopping for graceful drain. Never Swagger in Production.'
introducedIn: IHostEnvironment since .NET Core 2.1; environment-based config since 1.0

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express checks NODE_ENV to enable view caching and disable verbose errors. ASP.NET Core IsDevelopment() is the parallel guard — but .NET defaults to Production, Node often does not.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: NestJS enable versioning and Swagger per environment
jsTsCorrelations.note: NestJS conditionally registers SwaggerModule in non-production — same pattern as if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment()) in Program.cs.
